title: the brigade is not cleaned before the backend connection goes back to the pool
live_proof: this corpus pins the allocators (APR 1.7.4, apr-util 1.6.3), not httpd; a case reproduces the call sequence rather than a shipped tree, and says so instead of asserting liveness
object: nodes from the connection's bucket allocator, still named by the brigade
lifetime_ender: the connection, and with it its bucket allocator, being handed back to the pool for the next request: upstream expresses this as a copying discipline, not as an allocator event; the reduced consumer expresses it as the lender's epoch (destroy and recreate the allocator at the handback), which the Sublet discipline requires of a lender that reuses without freeing
shape: a recycled allocator serving its next user
allocator_layer: apr_bucket_alloc_t over apr_pool_t over apr_allocator_t -- two recycling levels, neither reaching malloc
fidelity: model-consumer, real allocators: apr_buckets_alloc.c and apr_pools.c are upstream byte for byte through the port's shims; brigades, filters, connections and requests are reduced to the holder and the storage

native-fix-differential.oracle: the buggy arm leaves storage named after its owner gave it back; the fixed arm does not
native-fix-differential.note: this pair differs by whether the upstream fix is applied, not by protection
native-fix-differential.measures: free() is interposed and counted, so freed_to_malloc is measured per case and not inherited from the census

cheribsd-revocation.target: stock CheriBSD purecap, libc heap revocation enabled
cheribsd-revocation.oracle: completes: no free happens at the handback and none in the reduced consumer's epoch reaches malloc, so the revoker has no event
cheribsd-revocation.measured: 2026-09-22 through the port's CheriBSD build: completed, exit 0; the run's revocation-control faulted at apr_defect_read (signal 34, code 2) in the same guest. 2026-09-21, census build with free() interposed: completed, freed_to_malloc=0
cheribsd-revocation.control: the run's cheribsd-abi probe prints CHERI_ABI pointer_bytes=16 runtime_revocation=1 from CheriBSD's own malloc_revoke_enabled(), in the same guest, immediately before these cases
cheribsd-revocation.guest_default: preserved -- nothing is disabled to make room for this measurement

spatial.oracle: complete: the block is reissued under the same alias, the stale read returns the next user's bytes

sublet.oracle: fault at the labelled read probe (cause 24, revoked authority): the handback is the lender's epoch, the allocator's blocks go back to APR and are reissued, and the old brigade's bucket alias dies with its block; no free happened, so this is the class-3 catch

native-detect.requires: neither level reaches malloc, so ASan has no event; Valgrind against APR's own annotations is the arm that could discriminate

status: run 2026-09-22 under QEMU through the port (ports/apr/pools with -DAPRP_BUCKETS=ON): spatial completes; sublet faults with cause 24 at the published apr_defect_read, the event being the connection handback, declared by the reduced consumer as the allocator's epoch: its blocks go back to APR and are reissued, the pool port's release; stock CheriBSD with libc revocation on completes, 2026-09-22 through the port and 2026-09-21 through the census build; results/20260922-qemu and results/20260922-cheribsd
note: the Capstone arms run the buggy sequence with protection as the variable; the fix differential is the native pair
taxonomy_class: 3, reuse-not-free: the lender reuses the connection and its allocator without freeing what the old request still names
distinguishing: the corpus's one reuse-not-free case: nothing is freed, the lender hands its connection and allocator to the next request. Under upstream's code the handback is no allocator event, so no free-triggered mechanism can see the stale brigade; the reduced consumer declares the handback as the allocator's epoch, which is what the Sublet discipline asks of a lender that reuses, and that declaration is the one step the reduced sequence takes that upstream does not
